Ultimately, in a lot of cases, it will be about seeing the hidden meaning beneath the bricks and mortar - peeling back the veil for a deeper experience. Anyone can walk, look, and even google / wiki; but every insight gain, every bit of non-obvious knowledge brings a deeper sense of connection and understanding of the place, whether new or already familiar.

I like the tone and the quirkyness of it but I think it should come after something just a litle more conventional. Ideally I would build around a factual anchor: the coaching inn. Start with the crossroads and where it came from (must be old roads, how old? Roman? medieval? where was it going to and from, for what, for who?), then it leading naturally to being a coaching station (tally ho), and then the quirky anecdote, and maybe something short about what it is today if anything remarkable and positive is found (I don't think that's the case for current day tally ho). Obviously that's a lot so we'd want to probably gauge how many of these we can / want to string together depending on how long we feel we have (and user preferences re. length and interests when we get to that)
